title: Quantum Week: FCA, Anthropic vs OpenAI, Stablecoin Shift

Regulators are experimenting with quantum machine learning to hunt fraudsters, AI labs are carving up the banking enterprise market, and the stablecoin supply just posted its sharpest contraction since 2022. Welcome to the week technology stopped being adjacent to finance and became the point of it. If you blinked this week, you missed roughly a decade of financial technology compression. The UK's top conduct regulator formally entered the quantum era. Anthropic and OpenAI squared off over the right to power the next generation of banking software. Hong Kong dropped a tokenisation framework with enough ambition to rattle London and Singapore. And stablecoins, the backbone of modern on-chain finance, shed more than $14 billion in a single month, the largest contraction since the 2022 bear market. If the question was "is finance about to become a software problem," this week was the answer: it already is, and the software just got weirder. The FCA Goes Quantum. Start with the headline that genuinely surprised a lot of practitioners. On November 5, the UK's Financial Conduct Authority ( FCA ) formally announced the launch of a Quantum Experimentation Group, with its first real-world use case focused on applying quantum machine learning to financial crime detection, according to the FCA's own press release and coverage from The Quantum Insider , Fintech Futures, and FS Tech. What the FCA actually said. The regulator isn't just running a thought experiment. The Quantum Experimentation Group will bring together UK universities, quantum hardware providers, and regulated firms to test whether quantum-enhanced machine learning models can meaningfully outperform classical approaches at detecting anomalies in transaction data, the raw material of fraud and anti-money-laundering detection, according to Regulation Tomorrow and A&O Shearman's FinReg bulletin. Why this matters: AML has been stuck in a well-documented productivity trap for years. Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) filings keep rising, false positive rates remain stubbornly high, and compliance teams burn through resources chasing noise. If quantum machine learning can genuinely compress that signal-to-noise problem, and that's still an open question, the economics of financial crime compliance change dramatically. The context nobody should ignore. The FCA move slots into a bigger regulatory shift. CMS 's recent analysis and the World Economic Forum 's work on quantum-secure financial sector regulation both point to the same conclusion: regulators are no longer treating quantum as a 2030+ problem. The combination of post-quantum cryptography migration deadlines and quantum ML experimentation means financial firms need a quantum strategy in 2027, not 2029. Expect other regulators, notably MAS (), the SEC , and BaFin , to publish their own quantum experimentation initiatives in the coming quarters. Anthropic vs OpenAI: The Banking Core Is Up for Grabs. While regulators fiddled with qubits, the AI labs continued their push into the banking enterprise. PYMNTS reports that Anthropic and OpenAI are now in an open race to capture what the headline calls "banking's services core", the system-of-work that supports operations, servicing, risk, and research across every major bank. What's new this week. Multiple sources confirm Anthropic has launched a dedicated enterprise finance unit, deploying a suite of bank-focused AI agents built in partnership with JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs , per coverage from PYMNTS, Pulse. bot , and The Paypers. The move follows Anthropic's reported $15 billion joint venture framework earlier this year. OpenAI, meanwhile, is making its own moves. American Banker reports BBVA and Goldman Sachs have both participated in OpenAI's new venture, while eMarketer separately reports that OpenAI is expanding into UK banks even as Anthropic restricts access to its newest frontier model, codenamed internally as Mythos. Once a bank brings an AI agent back online to help with fraud reviews, its first case file could look much like the ones analysts saw before the attack. Would the analyst reviewing it spot a missed transaction check?. A backup might contain an older copy of the model, while the script for preparing its data was updated later. The team can recover both pieces and still have to work out whether they ever ran together. Commvault calls that missing history the context gap in its June 2026 report on AI agent recovery, The AI Resilience Blueprint. How a False Detail Ends Up in a Fraud Case. Two agents might put the file together, one pulling the transaction history and account notes while the other writes the summary. An altered note can make it through both agents and turn up as evidence. Agents that remember earlier tasks may carry the detail into later cases. With write access, they could save it in a system other teams use. What Could a Bank’s Backups Leave Out?. Account notes may sit in a separate database while the model runs on a managed cloud service. Having a backup of the model leaves the bank to check whether it can also recover the notes the agent relies on. Self-hosted model registries can sit outside that coverage, too, the report notes. The report asks banks to trace the source and handling of training data because tampering can change how the model behaves once it goes live. Restoring the model and data can leave an attacker’s changes to the agent’s permissions in place. Before reconnecting the agent to customer systems, the team needs to check what it can read or change against the access the bank originally approved. How Does a Bank Know Which Setup to Restore?. The recovery team can look up the version the bank deployed in the model registry, then match it to the data, instructions and permissions the agent used at the time. Commvault’s report proposes using a system of record for AI agent recovery to tie those details together at a given time. Paired with logs of what agents read and handed off, it could help the bank see which cases relied on an altered note. Knowing when the note first turned up gives the team a point to work back from. Isolated backups that preserve earlier versions and are protected against tampering can help the bank find a combination of software, data and settings that ran together. The report calls the target a known-good state, a setup the team can verify before using it again. What to Test Before an Agent Goes Live Again. title: Banks on notice as Australians consult AI to help choose their lender
excerpt: James Eyers Senior Reporter. Nov 15, 2026 – 8. 00pm. or Subscribe to save article. Email LinkedIn Twitter Facebook. Subscribe to gift this article. Gift articles to anyone you choose each month when you subscribe. Subscribe now Already a subscriber?. For many years, prospective bank customers have used a search engine like Google to help them decide who to borrow from. These days, it’s more likely they will have conversed with artificial intelligence for guidance. For banks and fintechs, that means efforts to make their brand more visible to search algorithms, a strategy known as search engine optimisation, are no longer enough. A new approach is required to ensure their name pops up in answers delivered by large language models such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude. The new techniques, sometimes known as “generative engine optimisation”, are set to have a major impact on lending volumes across the finance sector. Customers will discover borrowing options by talking to AI through different stages of the product journey, from education to exploration, evaluation and selection. “It’s like being back in 1998 before the internet came out, before Google existed. That’s where we’re at,” said Jeremy Liddle, executive chair of Third Hemisphere. “But we’re going to go through five years of what happened in the dotcom era in the next six to 12 months. ”. His firm is developing a series of ‘AI authority’ indexes to show where and how brands appear in AI-generated responses to questions such as ‘which credit card lenders are best and worst?’ or ‘what is the best mortgage product?’. Advertisement. “AI SEO is being invented right now. It’s the wild west. And the companies that invest in it early will be light years in front when AI agents actively start making decisions on behalf of buyers,” Liddle said. In each conversation with its user, an AI model scours the internet for brand sentiment in seconds. It ingests content including media articles, comparison sites, lists of awards, customer reviews on social media and company webpages, forming a picture presented to the customer as a natural conversation. Third Hemisphere’s AI authority index for personal lending collected over 154,791 answers, after asking 166 questions across five engines: ChatGPT, Claude, Google’s Gemini, Microsoft’s Copilot and Perplexity. Scores were allocated based on how consistently a lender was named, combining reputation, influence, presence and the readability for AI of corporate websites. Commonwealth Bank was the clear winner in searches for personal loans, including credit cards, while ANZ was a laggard among the big four. ING and fintechs like OurMoneyMarket, Plenti and Harmoney scored ahead of NAB, Westpac, Macquarie and ANZ on reputation. Advertisement. One of the challenges of AI search is customers using more nuanced and subjective questions than traditional search: for example, ‘which credit card can I trust, and who should I avoid’ or ‘I have a bad credit rating and I want to consolidate my debt, which lenders are best and worst?’ This forces the models to look for positive and negative views. “Using Gemini or Grok on your phone is becoming the starting point in the buying journey,” said Dan Jones, who leads the digital practice at consultancy firm Oliver Wyman. “Customers are using compare and contrast prompts and asking for pros and cons of doing something – and there is a big difference in how banks are showing up in large language model results. “This is an opportunity to get clever on how a product works and to articulate simpler terms and conditions to capture attention. Banks also need to make it easier to move to the next step, when the customer asks: what do I do next?”. The models look for unbiased information with authority. title: Aton launches digital power of attorney for banks, allowing AI transfers of up to 100,000 won
excerpt: Aton launches digital power of attorney for banks, allowing AI transfers of up to 100,000 won. Aton unveiled an authentication solution that verifies the authority and limits delegated to an AI agent when it conducts transfers or payments on behalf of a customer. On Thursday, Aton announced the official launch of its AI agent authentication and signature verification solution, 'AI AgentSign,' marking its entry into the financial sector's AI agent authentication market. AI AgentSign issues certificates in the form of digital powers of attorney that authenticate the authority delegated by customers to AI agents. Much like a person gives a proxy a written authorization specifying monetary limits, AI agents are granted a 'digital power of attorney. '. When a customer sets per-transaction and daily transaction limits in an app and signs the delegation consent form with a PIN, a certificate dedicated to the AI agent is issued. The transaction limits are recorded on the certificate itself. Each time an AI requests a transfer or payment, the system verifies whether that specific agent has been legitimately delegated authority by the customer and whether the transaction falls within the permitted scope. Transactions are blocked if an electronic signature is missing or if the request details have been altered. For example, if a customer grants an AI agent the authority to make transfers of up to 100,000 won per transaction, the AI can directly process a transfer of 50,000 won. Transactions exceeding 100,000 won require a separate approval request sent to the customer's mobile phone and a PIN signature before execution. If the customer revokes the delegation in the app, the corresponding certificate is immediately discarded. Aton explained that connecting AI with financial systems using only existing API keys or tokens makes it difficult to verify exactly what authority a customer has delegated. It also noted limitations in verifying cases where keys are stolen or request details are tampered with. AI AgentSign applies certificate and electronic signature specifications based on the international standards X. 509 and CMS. The AI agent's signing key is stored in Aton's 'Quantum SafeBOX,' a secure medium based on post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and white-box encryption. Aton is currently in discussions with multiple financial institutions regarding the adoption of AI AgentSign. The company plans to expand its scope of application, starting with transfers and payments by AI agents within financial apps, to payment integration for external AI services and role-based authority delegation for enterprise business AI. Woo Gil-soo, CEO of Aton, stated, "In an era where AI moves money on behalf of customers, trust mechanisms that prove who the AI is and what it has been authorized to do must be established first. title: Autonomous treasury agents: How Trovata built an AI-native solution on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore
excerpt: Autonomous treasury agents: How Trovata built an AI-native solution on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore. Corporate treasury teams face a persistent challenge: fragmented banking data scattered across dozens of bank portals, manual reporting trapped in spreadsheets, and legacy Treasury Management Systems (TMS) that can’t scale for modern enterprise needs. For treasury teams these manual processes create delays, errors, and an inability to make real-time cash decisions when they matter most. Trovata is an AI-native cash and liquidity management platform with direct connections to over 10,000 banks, serving enterprises globally from a single cloud-based platform. In 2023, Trovata launched the first generative AI built specifically for treasury. Now, with Trovata’s latest AI-native updates, they’ve evolved from delivering insights to deploying autonomous agents that act on behalf of treasury teams. Trovata’s customers have seen measurable results: $1M+ in annualized cost savings, over 5 hours per day saved per accounting team, a 77 percent reduction in annual TMS costs, and treasury reporting reduced from hours or days to under a minute. In this post, we explore how Trovata built autonomous treasury agents on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, the architecture secured with role-based access control (RBAC) that supports bank-branded AI deployment, and how agentic workflows are transforming corporate treasury from manual operations to real-time decision-making at enterprise scale. Solution overview. Trovata operates as an AI-native treasury operating system, providing direct connections to over 10,000 banks through a single system for cash reporting, forecasting, analysis, and money movement. Treasury teams today face a three-pressure problem:. Fragmented banking data across multiple portals, requiring manual aggregation and reconciliation. Manual reporting and reconciliation consuming hours or even days of skilled team members’ time. Legacy TMS applications that lack cloud-native architecture and AI capabilities needed for modern operations. Trovata’s evolution from its first generative AI for treasury in 2023 to its AI-native capabilities with autonomous agents represents a fundamental shift. The solution moves from static insights to persistent agentic workflows that operate continuously on behalf of treasury teams. Critically, Trovata AI is built directly into the treasury operating system. It’s not a generic chatbot layered on top, but embedded intelligence tied to real treasury objects with a governed path to automation through agents. Trovata chose AWS for this transformation for three reasons. Its serverless, cloud-native infrastructure supports real-time execution, Amazon Bedrock provides large language model (LLM) inference for natural language queries and AI features, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore handles agent orchestration with RBAC security, rapid deployment, and global scale. The core AWS services powering Trovata’s AI-native solution include:. Amazon Bedrock – LLM inference for natural language understanding and generation. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore – Agent orchestration, agentic workflows, and RBAC security. Serverless AWS infrastructure – Real-time execution at enterprise scale. Architecture diagram. The Trovata AI architecture centers on autonomous treasury agents operating within a bank-branded, RBAC-secured framework. The solution comprises several key components working together:. Trovata AI Chat – Natural language querying of multi-bank treasury data, so users can ask questions like “What was our net cash position across all accounts yesterday?” and receive instant, accurate responses. AI Insights – Automated anomaly detection, variance explanation, and trend analysis that surfaces critical information proactively. AI Agents – Persistent workflows running on schedules, triggers, or rules to monitor activity, explain variance, detect anomalies, and deliver updates automatically, without human intervention.
